overview: Early-medieval north (Harsha, Palas) and the south Indian dynasties: 27 official questions (2008-2024), led by Harsha/Kanauj (7), Badami Chalukyas with Pallavas (5), Cholas (5) and Kakatiyas (4). 19 are one-liners on titles, authors, founders and terms; matching and wrong-pair items appear since 2023. Hoysalas, Yadavas and Reddis are not yet asked.

possibility.angle: Harsha, Kanauj and the Pala universities
possibility.what_they_ask: titles (Siladitya); court poet Bana; traveller-ruler pairs; Nalanda under Harsha; who founded Vikramashila; Atisha to Tibet
Pallava king titles and works (Mahendravarman); Pulakesin II vs Harsha; Pallava-Chalukya wars; ghatikas
titles of Vengi kings; Chola marriage alliance; ghatikas
founder, Kailasa builder, Kavirajamarga, Arab accounts (Balhara)
Vijnaneswara's Mitakshara at Vikramaditya VI's court
village terms (taniyur, variyam); founder and conquests of each king; Dravida style; temple colleges
works and the reign they belong to (Nritta Ratnavali); Telugu translations (Ketana); ruler-event matching; trade routes
natural targets: capital Dwarasamudra (Halebidu), Vishnuvardhana and Ramanuja, Belur/Halebidu/Somanathapura temples, Vesara style
natural targets: capital Devagiri, Singhana, Hemadri (minister, Hemadpanti style), Ramachandra's defeat by Alauddin's forces
natural targets: Prolaya Vema Reddi founder, capitals Addanki then Kondavidu, Rajahmundry branch, Srinatha at Pedakomati Vema's court

traps.trap: [Same name, other king] Title given to the wrong king of the same name
traps.spot: Options list Pulakesin I/II or Mahendravarman I/II, Narasimhavarman I/II
traps.fix: Attach the title to the event: Parameshvara after beating Harsha = Pulakesin II; Vichitrachitta = Mahendravarman I
traps.pyq: 'Who defeated Harsha and assumed the title Parameshwar' → Pulakesin II [group1-prelims-2010#9]; Vichitrachitta → Mahendravarman [group1-prelims-2010#112]

traps.trap: Founder swapped with a famous later king
traps.spot: 'X was founded by' with a well-known conqueror's name
traps.fix: Imperial Cholas = Vijayalaya; Rashtrakutas = Dantidurga; Vikramashila = Dharmapala; Nalanda = Kumaragupta I
traps.pyq: 'Chola Empire was founded by Parantaka-I' → Vijayalaya [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#12]; Dharmapala → Vikramasila [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#147]

traps.trap: Monument credited to the wrong king of the dynasty
traps.spot: Kailasa, Ellora with Krishna III or Amoghavarsha
traps.fix: Kailasa = Krishna I; Krishna III is the Kanchi/Tanjore raider
traps.pyq: 'Krishna-III : rock-cut temple of Shiva at Ellora' → Krishna I [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#11]

traps.trap: Traveller placed in the wrong reign
traps.fix: Megasthenes-Chandragupta Maurya; Fa-Hien-Chandragupta II; Xuanzang-Harsha; I-Tsing 671-695

traps.trap: Inflated numbers and wrong language for Nalanda
traps.spot: Statements with big numbers (10,000 villages, 15,000 teachers) or 'Pali medium'
traps.fix: About 100-200 villages, about 1,510 teachers, Sanskrit medium, Silabhadra at the head
traps.pyq: Only 'Silabhadra was the Chancellor' is correct [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#9]

traps.trap: Work placed in the wrong Kakatiya reign
traps.spot: Kakatiya text asked with all four rulers as options
traps.fix: Nritta Ratnavali by Jayapa = Ganapatideva's reign; Prataparudriyam = Prataparudra

traps.trap: Institution of one religion given to another
traps.spot: Ghatika described as Buddhist centre or as a village
traps.fix: Ghatika = Brahmanical college (Sanskrit); vihara = Buddhist; agrahara = Brahmin village
traps.pyq: 'Ghatikas were' → Hindu colleges [group1-prelims-2008#10]; settlement of Brahmin scholars [group1-prelims-2012#48]

techniques.name: Event-tied title recall
techniques.how: [Title ← event] Do not memorise titles alone; link each to the event that earned it, then match the event to the king.
techniques.example: 'Parameshwar' was taken after defeating Harsha on the Narmada → Pulakesin II, not Pulakesin I (founder) or the Pallavas [group1-prelims-2010#9]

techniques.name: Century gap elimination
techniques.how: Put a century next to each traveller, author or king; a pair separated by centuries is the wrong one.
techniques.example: I-Tsing (7th c. AD) vs Ashoka (3rd c. BC) → wrong pair; the other three are contemporaries [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#2]

techniques.name: Pallava-Chalukya swing chart
techniques.how: Remember the back-and-forth: Pulakesin II beats Mahendravarman I; Narasimhavarman I takes Vatapi 642; Vikramaditya II takes Kanchi under Nandivarman II.
techniques.example: Narasimhavarman I → destruction of Vatapi; Nandivarman II → Kanchi captured; Vishnugopa → Samudragupta → 'A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#10]

techniques.name: Dynasty fact row for wrong-pair items
techniques.how: For each dynasty keep a row: founder - capital - great builder - literary king - last king; test each option against the row.
techniques.example: Rashtrakuta row: Dantidurga founder, Krishna I Kailasa, Amoghavarsha Kavirajamarga → Krishna III pair is wrong [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#11]

techniques.name: Author-to-court link
techniques.how: Fix where each author worked; the court gives the ruler and the period.
techniques.example: Mitakshara by Vijnaneswara at Vikramaditya VI's court is a commentary on Yajnavalkya Smriti [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#1]; Bana → Harsha [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#15]

confusions.remember: Mahendra = Vichitrachitta, Mattavilasa author; Narasimha I = Mamalla, took Vatapi 642
I founded Badami; II beat Harsha, Aihole inscription
I = Kailasa, Ellora; III = raids on Kanchi and Tanjore
Vijayalaya founded imperial Cholas c.850; Parantaka I = Maduraikonda
Rajaraja = Maldives, Sri Lanka, Brihadisvara; Rajendra = Gangaikondacholapuram, Kedah
Vishamasiddhi, Vengi founder 624 vs Tripuramartya Maheswara
Ketana = Mitakshara into Telugu (Vijnaneswaramu); Baddena = Sumati Satakam
Fa-Hien = Chandragupta II; Xuanzang = Harsha, Nalanda under Silabhadra
Brahmanical college vs Buddhist monastery / Brahmin village

anchors: Harsha 606-647 = Siladitya; court poet Bana (Harshacharita, Kadambari)
Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada; title Parameshvara (Aihole)
Vengi: Kubja Vishnuvardhana founded the Eastern Chalukya line in 624
Rashtrakutas: Dantidurga founder; Krishna I Kailasa; Amoghavarsha Kavirajamarga
Cholas: Vijayalaya founder c.850; Rajendra I Gangaikondacholapuram
Chola village: variyam = committee, kudavolai = pot-ticket lottery, taniyur = big village as its own unit
Kakatiyas: Thousand Pillar Temple 1163 (Rudradeva); Marco Polo under Rudramadevi; Malik Kafur under Prataparudra
Nalanda in Harsha's time: Silabhadra head, Sanskrit medium
Dravida = south, Nagara = north, Vesara = Deccan
checklist: Same-name kings in the options? Decide by the event, not by the name.
Founder questions: the founder is rarely the most famous king.
Put a century on each pair in traveller/author questions.
Big round numbers in a statement: check against the actual figure.
For a work, find the court first, then the ruler.
Read the key note mentally: some Chola and Kakatiya matching keys are disputed - do not over-learn them.
